question: What is the primary definition of rational drug use?

options.A: Ensuring every patient takes at least five different medications daily
options.B: Receiving appropriate medications suited to individual clinical needs at the lowest cost
options.C: Prescribing the newest and most expensive drugs available on the market
options.D: Administering drugs exclusively via the intravenous route for faster relief

explanation: Rational drug use focuses on matching the right drug and dose to the specific clinical needs of the patient affordably. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h1)

question: According to WHO guidelines, what must precede the prescription of any therapeutic agent?

options.A: Expiration date verification by the pharmacist
options.B: A valid clinical diagnosis justifying the choice
options.C: Approval from a hospital financial officer
options.D: Patient request for a specific brand name

explanation: Appropriate indication requires that a clear diagnosis justifies why a specific medication is being given. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which principle of rational drug use addresses checking for patient allergies and physiological contraindications?
explanation: Evaluating the appropriate patient involves screening for personal risk factors like existing allergies or organ dysfunction. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is polypharmacy?

options.A: The practice of buying drugs exclusively from wholesale markets
options.B: The administration of drugs only through intravenous infusions
options.C: The concurrent use of multiple medications by a single patient
options.D: The manufacturing of fake pharmaceutical products in local shops

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to taking multiple medications at the same time, which raises the risk of drug interactions. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is a major clinical risk associated with the overuse of antibiotics?

options.A: Development of antimicrobial resistance making infections harder to treat
options.B: Significant decrease in normal human body temperature
options.C: Immediate and permanent blindness in all affected patients
options.D: Complete regeneration of damaged kidney tissue

explanation: Overusing antibiotics allows bacteria to adapt and survive, leading to resistant strains that standard drugs cannot clear. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h3)

question: When does medication reconciliation typically take place in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Exclusively after a surgical procedure has been completed
options.B: Only when a patient is being discharged to a nursing home
options.C: During transitions of care such as admission, transfer, and discharge
options.D: Whenever a physician decides to increase a patient drug dosage

explanation: Reconciliation happens whenever care is transferred to ensure medication lists remain accurate at every step. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why must nurses inquire about herbal remedies and supplements during a medication history interview?

options.A: Hospital pharmacies require herbal supplements to stock their main shelves
options.B: Government regulations mandate that herbal remedies replace all antibiotics
options.C: Supplements always enhance the speed of surgical wound healing
options.D: Herbs can cause unexpected pharmacokinetic interactions or toxicity with orthodox drugs

explanation: Patients often forget that herbs are pharmacologically active and can interact dangerously with prescribed medications. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is a common barrier to medication adherence among patients?

options.A: Complex dosing schedules and bothersome side effects
options.B: Complete absence of any chronic health conditions
options.C: Having too many free medications supplied at home
options.D: Instantaneous and painless recovery from illness

explanation: Difficult regimens and unpleasant side effects frequently discourage patients from taking their medications consistently. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h5)

question: How can nurses effectively support adherence in patients with low health literacy?

options.A: Withholding all instructions until the patient asks specific questions
options.B: Handing out lengthy academic medical journals for independent reading
options.C: Speaking exclusively in complex medical jargon to establish authority
options.D: Using simplified language, pictorial aids, and involving family caregivers

explanation: Plain language and visual aids make complex drug regimens understandable and manageable for patients and families. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of pharmacovigilance?

options.A: Advertising new pharmaceutical products to healthcare providers
options.B: Detecting, assessing, and preventing adverse effects and drug-related problems
options.C: Increasing the manufacturing speed of essential painkillers
options.D: Determining the wholesale market price of imported medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance monitors drug safety continuously after release to catch and prevent harmful reactions. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which agency in Nigeria is primarily responsible for receiving spontaneous adverse drug reaction reports?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing

explanation: NAFDAC regulates drug safety and manages the pharmacovigilance system for reporting adverse reactions in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which strategy directly helps reduce medication errors in a hospital setting?

options.A: Allowing patients to dispense their own drugs without supervision
options.B: Multidisciplinary medication reviews and stewardship programs
options.C: Eliminating all nursing documentation during night shifts
options.D: Using unlabelled containers for emergency medications

explanation: Collaborative reviews and structured stewardship programs catch prescribing mistakes and promote safe drug use. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is NOT a recommended action for a nurse when facing an ambiguous medication order?

options.A: Clarifying the order with the prescribing physician before administration
options.B: Administering the drug immediately and guessing the correct dose later
options.C: Consulting the clinical pharmacist for verification of safety limits
options.D: Reviewing current hospital treatment guidelines and protocols

explanation: Guessing doses puts patients at extreme risk; unclear orders must always be clarified before administration. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h7)
